# Roy Gardner

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v3 c6 P27](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0027), [v3 c25 P36](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0036)</sub>
- **Origin:** Kingsport  <sub>[v3 c4 P30](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0030), [v3 c6 P8](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0008)</sub>
- **Role:** Student and magazine writer  <sub>[v3 c4 P36](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0036), [v3 c23 P21](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0021)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Roy  <sub>[v3 c6 P8](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

Roy Gardner is an exceptionally handsome, tall, and broad-shouldered man with a distinguished-looking appearance. He has a finely-cut nose and chin, large, brilliant, dark-gray eyes, and thick brown hair. He dresses with elegant, highbred taste and possesses a delightful, pleading voice and a charming smile.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P43](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0043), [v3 c23 P28](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0028), [v3 c25 P28](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0028), [v3 c25 P29](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0029), [v3 c25 P33](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0033), [v3 c25 P48](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0048)_

## Personality

Roy is a romantic, cultured, and soft-spoken gentleman who expresses his feelings through poetry, flowers, and chivalrous gestures. He is deeply devoted to his mother, deferring his college education for two years to travel with her when her health failed. While well-mannered and sincere in his affections, he lacks a strong sense of humor, which can make his conversation feel slightly dull or uninteresting to those looking for fun. When his romantic proposals are rejected, he feels things intensely at the time, though he eventually recovers and finds love elsewhere.

_Sources: [v3 c23 P15](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0015), [v3 c25 P32](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0032), [v3 c25 P42](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0042), [v3 c25 P48](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0048), [v3 c27 P33](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0033), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v3 c38 P18](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0018), [v3 c38 P25](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0025), [v3 c38 P28](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0028), [v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032), [v3 c39 P2](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0002), [v3 c39 P5](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0005)_

## History

Royal Gardner was born in Kingsport to a wealthy and aristocratic family. After completing his Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond College, he was forced to pause his studies to accompany his ill mother to Europe for two years. Upon returning to Redmond to finish his Arts degree, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a heavy November rainstorm, rescuing her with his umbrella. He fell deeply in love with Anne, courting her over the next two years with flowers, poetry, and dedicated attentions, causing college circles to assume they would marry. In their Senior year, he brought his mother and sisters to meet Anne at Patty's Place. At the end of their college career, Roy proposed to Anne in the park pavilion where they had first met, but she unexpectedly rejected his proposal upon realizing she did not truly love him. A year later, Roy married another girl and subsequently achieved great literary success by writing a famous novel based on Captain Jim Boyd's life-book, which he composed while spending a summer at Four Winds Harbor.

## Quotes

> Pardon me—may I offer you the shelter of my umbrella?  <sub>[v3 c25 P27](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0027)</sub>

> I feel as if I didn't belong anywhere yet. I put in my Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond two years ago. I've been in Europe ever since. Now I've come back to finish my Arts course.  <sub>[v3 c25 P38](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0038)</sub>

> Anne, I love you. You know I do. I—I can't tell you how much. Will you promise me that some day you'll be my wife?  <sub>[v3 c38 P31](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0031)</sub>

> You have ruined my life.  <sub>[v3 c38 P27](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0027)</sub>

> Good-bye, Anne. I can't understand it—I can't believe you are not the woman I've believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne.  <sub>[v3 c38 P32](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0032)</sub>
